name: Runekit COD Guard for WooCommerce
author: runekit

sections.description:
Every refused cash on delivery (COD) parcel costs you shipping twice. Runekit COD Guard gives you real COD rules in the free plugin, with nothing locked:

  • Order total limits for COD: a minimum and a maximum order total for cash on delivery. Above your maximum, customers simply pay online.
  • COD only where you deliver it: allow COD only for listed cities, regions/states or postcodes (wildcards like 115* and ranges like 11000...11999). City names match in Arabic and English, and Arabic spelling variants (أ/إ/ا, ة/ه, ى/ي, “ال”) are matched automatically.
  • Blocklists for phones, emails and IPs: one phone entry matches every format (0501234567, +966 50 123 4567, 00966501234567, Arabic digits). Block an email, a whole @domain, an IP or a CIDR range. Gmail dots and +tags cannot be used to slip past the list.
  • Daily COD limit per phone: stop the same number placing many COD orders in 24 hours.
  • “Refused (COD)” order status with memory: mark a parcel the customer refused, and after the number of refusals you choose, their phone and email are added to the COD blocklist automatically. Works from the order screen and as a bulk action.
  • One-click “block this customer” from the order actions menu.
  • Only COD is affected: blocked customers still see your online payment methods, so you never lose a prepaid sale.
  • COD Guard box on every order showing the normalised phone, earlier refusals and which rules the order fails.

Built for COD-heavy stores in Saudi Arabia, the Gulf, Egypt, North Africa, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. Works with the classic checkout and the Cart and Checkout blocks, and is compatible with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS). The admin is fully translatable through WordPress.org and every screen works in right-to-left mode.

Privacy: the plugin makes no external requests, loads no remote files and does no tracking. All checks use data already in your store.

COD Guard Pro (optional)

A separate paid add-on, for stores that want more than rules:

  • Risk score (0-100) for every new COD order, from local signals only (earlier refusals, repeat orders from the same phone or IP, completed-order history, address and name checks).
  • Auto-hold risky COD orders as “On hold” until you confirm them.
  • Optional deposit (a partial prepayment of the order price, with no added fee or interest) for risky COD orders, paid online with your existing gateways, then credited against the amount collected on delivery.
  • WhatsApp confirmation links: one click opens WhatsApp on your own phone with an Arabic or English message ready to send. No paid messaging service.
  • Refusal history per customer on the order screen.

The free plugin is complete on its own and never asks you to upgrade.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce and enable the “Cash on delivery” payment method.
  2. Install Runekit COD Guard from Plugins > Add New, or upload the zip, and activate it.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > COD Guard and set your rules and blocklists.
  4. Optional: set your default country calling code under COD Guard > Advanced if your customers use numbers from another country.
sections.faq:
Will this block all my orders?

No. Only the Cash on delivery method is ever hidden, and only for checkouts that fail a rule you set. With no rules set, nothing changes. Other payment methods are never touched.

What happens if a blocked customer still picks COD?

If COD was already showing (for example before they typed their phone), the order is stopped at “Place order” with a clear message asking them to choose another payment method. You can change the message under Advanced.

How are phone numbers matched?

Numbers are turned into one international form using your store country’s calling code, so 0501234567, +966501234567, 00966 50 123 4567 and ٠٥٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧ are the same number.

Does it work with the Checkout block and HPOS?

Yes, both. The plugin declares compatibility with High-Performance Order Storage and the Cart and Checkout blocks.

If several location lists are filled in, how do they combine?

COD is allowed when the address matches any one of the filled lists (cities, regions or postcodes). Leave a list empty to ignore it.

Does the plugin send data anywhere?

No. There are no external requests, no tracking and no remote files.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Settings are always removed. If you tick “Remove all data on uninstall” under Advanced, COD Guard’s order data is also removed and orders in “Refused (COD)” are moved to “Failed” so they stay visible.

What happens to “Refused (COD)” orders if I deactivate the plugin?

While the plugin is inactive, WooCommerce does not know the “Refused (COD)” status, so those orders are hidden from the order list until you reactivate it. Change them to another status first if you plan to remove the plugin for good, or tick “Remove all data on uninstall”.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First release: COD order total limits, allowed cities/regions/postcodes, phone/email/IP blocklists with phone normalisation, daily COD limit per phone, Refused (COD) status with auto-block, block-customer order action, HPOS and Checkout block support, translation-ready with RTL support.
